part_b.answer: 1. Kneser-Ney Smoothing is a type of smoothing technique that takes into account the frequency of words in the training data. 2. It uses a combination of back-off and interpolation to estimate the probability of a word given a context. 3. This approach is more accurate than other smoothing techniques in predicting the probability of rare words. 4. Kneser-Ney Smoothing is particularly useful in large language models where the frequency of words is skewed. 5. It is also more computationally efficient than other smoothing techniques. 6. The technique has been widely used in speech recognition and natural language processing applications. 7. However, it can be sensitive to the choice of parameters and the quality of the training data.
